count.split carries {exactText} then {relatedText} in both locales, one each, same order, middot kept; count.match, count.related and count.truncated carry {count, countText} in both. The only structural difference remains es's extra `many` arm, which is a category of this locale, not a divergence from the English arguments.

Beyond the diff proof (one line per in-scope file, at the count.split key), all 22 non-split values in both locales are byte-identical to the strings the round-1 receipt audited, including the two keys F-2 and F-3 name.

The new split keeps U+00B7 with plain spaces and no NBSP, colon immediately after the label with no space before it, and no new non-ASCII code points. Capitalising the second label after the middot starts a new label segment, which is how Spanish dashboards write label pairs, and it mirrors the English change.

counts_scope: Outstanding across the 23 keys after round 2. No new finding was raised in this round: the MAJOR is gone (F-1 resolved), and the MINOR and NIT are the two round-1 items whose bytes did not change (notes F-2, F-3). With no BLOCKER or MAJOR remaining the delta passes; the two open items are polish, and leaving them is a decision the wave may take explicitly.

notes.why: This is the fix round 1 proposed, and it holds up when checked against the reasoning rather than the diff: the line renders whenever both tiers are present, so either number can be 1, and a numeral directly beside an agreeing adjective cannot satisfy both at once. With the label first and the number after a colon, 'Exactas: 1' is a label with a count (the Spanish dashboard form, like 'Pendientes: 1'), not a numeral modifying an adjective, so the singular case no longer breaks anything. Rendered at 1/1, 1/3 and 7/1 with intl-messageformat: 'Exactas: 1 · Relacionadas: 1', 'Exactas: 1 · Relacionadas: 3', 'Exactas: 7 · Relacionadas: 1'. Placeholders, their order and the middot are intact, and the English side changed with it, so both languages now say the same thing in the same shape.

notes.prior_text: {count, plural, one {(la primera coincidencia mostrada)} many {(primeras {countText} mostradas)} other {(primeras {countText} mostradas)}}
notes.why: The es bytes did not move, so the finding is not resolved and is not withdrawn. The counter-consideration is worth naming: the English plural arm is itself article-less ('(first {countText} shown)', while its singular arm has 'the'), so es is mirroring the source shape faithfully, singular 'la' against plural bare. The suggestion stands as polish - '(las primeras {countText} mostradas)' - and it cannot block: it breaks no meaning, no placeholder and no pinned budget.

notes.prior_text: Puede que falten mensajes recientes mientras el índice se pone al día.
notes.why: Unchanged, so the comparative is still flattened ('recientes' for 'newer'). Non-blocking by definition of a NIT; 'los mensajes más recientes' would restore it if the wave touches the line again.
